items.title: Captain Verne Streckfus Interview, 1960-09-22
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] The Press made one record where it's guitar player Lonnie Johnson played violin. ... [INTERVIEWEE] I don't think they were outstanding to an extent that he just trained them and they were good for him, but they weren't good for anybody else.

ctx.x: And in the early days when they had this orchestra on the J.S. From the little Charlie Herzog. He played the violin in the early days. Otherwise, not much on the violin. You couldn't hear it for one thing. And if you played the band, they were soft enough that you could hear the violin. And they couldn't dance to it. That was before amplification. And then, played it on, but I just never really get back to violin.

The Press made one record where it's guitar player Lonnie Johnson played violin. I don't remember that. Dead sure. That's funny. I can't remember the people who played the track. I just haven't thought about it for a while.
I don't think they were outstanding to an extent that he just trained them and they were good for him, but they weren't good for anybody else. I don't know.
